WRITING ADVENTURES

Thirty pencil-control games, played with a finger or a stylus.

Real on-screen tracing: winding paths, loops, waves, zigzags, spirals, mazes, dot-to-dots and shape outlines — each with its own goal, gentle feedback and a worksheet to print. Works with touch, Apple Pencil, stylus, mouse and trackpad.

This way to Class 27 →The class that goes with these adventures: Early Writing & Pencil Control.

1. Curves and Paths

Six friendly roads to trace — winding, looping, waving, zigzagging, spiralling and arching over the rainbow.

1 Cleared! Hedgehog’s Winding PathTrace the winding road from the hedgehog to the strawberry.Wavy pencil control Play → 2 Cleared! Busy Bee Loop PracticeTrace the connected loops from the bee to the flowers.Loop and curve control Play → 3 Cleared! Sailboat Wave TracingDraw three smooth waves to carry the boat to the lighthouse.Smooth waves up and down Play → 4 Cleared! Rocket Zigzag MissionTrace the rocket’s zigzag flight up to the planet.Sharp zigzag strokes Play → 5 Cleared! Snail Spiral DrawingTrace the big spiral on the snail’s shell, from the middle outwards.Growing spirals Play → 6 Cleared! Rainbow Arch TracingDraw each rainbow band — four calm arches from cloud to cloud.Big curved arches Play →

2. Lines and Direction

Straight lines with a purpose — build a spider web, solve a maze, connect dots and march through the safari.

7 Cleared! Spider Web BuilderConnect the anchor points with straight strokes to build the web.Straight strokes between points Play → 8 Cleared! Puppy Maze AdventureDraw one continuous route from the puppy’s gate to the bone — without touching the walls.Planned routes and control Play → 9 Cleared! Ladybug Dot-to-DotConnect the ten numbered dots in order — 1, 2, 3… all the way to 10.Number order and connecting Play → 10 Cleared! Safari Line DrawingPractice tall lines, flat lines and slanted lines — one animal friend per kind.Vertical, horizontal and diagonal strokes Play → 11 Cleared! Octopus Curly ArmsDraw six curly tentacles, one friendly curl at a time.Curves that curl Play → 12 Cleared! Pencil Stroke AcademyFour exercises, four kinds of strokes: tall, flat, slanted and round.The four handwriting strokes Play →

3. Connect and Complete

Connect the points, trace the bones, sew the patch and skate the eight — careful, meaningful lines.

13 Cleared! Castle Bridge BuilderDraw the missing bridge planks from tower to tower.Straight horizontal strokes Play → 14 Cleared! Lion’s Crazy ManeDraw the mane: short strokes, long strokes and wavy strokes all around.Radiating strokes Play → 15 Cleared! Rainy Day DrawingTrace the rain: short drops, long drops and slanted drops.Short, long and slanted strokes Play → 16 Cleared! Dinosaur Fossil ArtistTrace the missing bone outlines to finish the dinosaur skeleton.Careful outline tracing Play → 17 Cleared! Teddy Bear Stitching StudioConnect the stitching dots to sew the patch onto the teddy’s tummy.Connecting points in order Play → 18 Cleared! Penguin Figure-Eight SkatingSkate one continuous figure-eight around the rink.Continuous loops crossing once Play → 19 Cleared! Little Railway EngineerDraw the two railway rails — two long parallel lines from station to station.Long parallel lines Play →

4. Shapes and Outlines

Shape drawing proper — arches, right angles, mirror wings, woolly humps, circles, rectangles, ovals, triangles and C-curves.

20 Cleared! Mountain Tent BuilderTrace the tent sides — slanted lines up to each peak and down.Diagonal strokes Play → 21 Cleared! Duckling Bridge ArchesDraw three arched bridges so the ducklings can cross the ponds.Semicircle arches Play → 22 Cleared! Robot Circuit WorkshopTrace the circuits — right angles only! — to power up the robot.Right-angle turns Play → 23 Cleared! Butterfly Mirror DrawingThe left wing is painted — draw the missing right wing to match it.Mirror symmetry Play → 24 Cleared! Fluffy Sheep Wool ArtistTrace the connected fluffy humps to grow the sheep’s wool.Connected bumps and humps Play → 25 Cleared! Giraffe Necklace DesignerTrace the big circle beads to finish the giraffe’s necklace.Full circles Play → 26 Cleared! Castle Brick ArtistTrace the missing bricks — careful rectangles that fit the wall.Rectangles Play → 27 Cleared! Squirrel Acorn DrawingTrace the oval acorn bodies for the squirrel’s winter store.Ovals Play → 28 Cleared! Pinwheel Shape MakerTrace the four triangle blades to finish the pinwheel.Triangles Play →

5. Creative Stroke Practice

The grand finale — creative stroke practice that pulls every skill together under the sun.

29 Cleared! Crab Claw CurvesTrace the C-shaped claw and the backwards-C claw.Open C curves Play → 30 Cleared! Sunshine Stroke ChallengeThe final challenge: twelve sun rays — short and long, all around.Mixed stroke lengths Play →

Every card opens one real tracing game. Progress — opened, completed and when — is saved on this device for the child chosen in My Classroom.

FOR GROWN-UPS

How the drawing works.

Each adventure shows the owner's original illustration with a transparent drawing layer laid right over it. The layer is aligned to the artwork's true pixel size, so a stroke lands exactly under the finger, the stylus or the mouse on every screen size and rotation — and because the picture itself is the activity, nothing on the page pretends to be a game.

Every page carries the same honest pencil case: nine crayons, an eraser, Undo, Redo and Clear, plus Save — and a child's adventure counts as cleared only when their finished picture is really saved. The worksheet twin still prints the same picture for away-from-screen practice.

The collection belongs to Class 27 — Early Writing & Pencil Control on the Age 4 path, beside Shape Adventures and Colors & Creativity.

PLAY · WAVY PENCIL CONTROL

Hedgehog’s Winding Path

Start at the green dot by the hedgehog and follow the winding road all the way to the strawberry.

Drawing on the picture needs JavaScript. Everything else on this page works without it — and the matching worksheet brings this adventure to paper.

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

This game builds wavy pencil control — one of the foundation strokes behind handwriting. Tracing a clear path with a finger or a stylus teaches speed, rhythm and control long before pencils arrive on paper, and the generous engine means an honest attempt is always celebrated. Watch for the moment the whole arm starts doing the work instead of the wrist — that is the real milestone.

Short, happy sessions of two or three adventures beat one long push, every time.

Tracing a clear path with a finger or a stylus teaches speed, rhythm and control long before pencils arrive on paper, and the generous engine means an honest attempt is always celebrated. Watch for the moment the whole arm starts doing the work instead of the wrist — that is the real milestone.

Short, happy sessions of two or three adventures beat one long push, every time.
